title: Step 1: Hook - A Story of Courage
text: Imagine living next to a large basketball court but being told, 'You cannot play because you are a girl.' This is exactly what happened to 13-year-old Afsana. She wanted to play, but there was a huge wall in front of her. Not a wall of bricks, but a wall made by society.

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
text: Have you ever wondered why some games are often called 'boys' games' and others 'girls' games'? What happens if a girl wants to play cricket, or a boy wants to play hopscotch? Think about what this invisible 'wall' stopping them could be made of.

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - Visualizing the Invisible Wall
content.description: This diagram shows a basketball court divided by a metaphorical barrier of societal expectations.

title: Step 4: Reveal - The Real Meaning of the Wall
text: The 'wall' Afsana crossed was the barrier of Gender Stereotypes. Society often builds rules dictating what boys and girls should do. Afsana, along with her friends Zarin, Khushnoor, and Afreen, broke this wall to form the Nagpada Basketball Association in Mumbai. They showed that talent and hard work matter, not gender.

content.definition: A fixed and oversimplified idea about how boys and girls should behave, play, or work.
The feeling of pride and loyalty that exists among the members of a team and that makes them want their team to do well or to be the best.

content.question: What does the 'wall' in the chapter 'Across the Wall' actually represent?
options: A tall boundary wall of the basketball court
Societal rules that stop girls from playing sports
A wall between two different cities

content.title: Did you know?
content.mistake: Thinking that a team's strength comes only from individual star players.
content.correction: Afsana's coach taught them that the real strength of a team is 'Team Spirit'. Even if every player is excellent, they can lose if they do not play together as one unit.

content.title: Step 6: Reflection
content.description: Look around your school playground or local park. Do boys and girls play together? Write down three reasons why it is important for everyone to play together, regardless of gender.

title: Step 7: Connection - From Court to Society
text: Playing sports together teaches us equality, respect, and cooperation. These are the same skills we need to build a better society. When boys and girls learn to support each other on the field, they grow up to support each other in workplaces, homes, and the country. Team spirit in sports is the foundation of unity in a nation.

content.title: Connecting to Ancient Indian Values
content.tip: Remind students that in ancient Indian texts like the Upanishads, the ultimate soul or 'Brahman' is beyond gender. True capability comes from the mind and spirit, not from being a boy or a girl.

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - Break Your Own Wall
content.description: Plan a mixed-gender sports match in your school or neighborhood. Work together to form teams where boys and girls pass the ball to each other and celebrate victories as one united team. Record your experience!
